text:
alex: Heads-up — since ~09:12 we're seeing repeated gRPC stream stalls between pods on different nodes in gpu-pool-usw2. High retransmits and fragmented packets in tcpdump. Suspect MTU/encap mismatch after last week's kernel bump. Anyone else seeing this? :frowning:

priya: Can you paste `ip link show` from one of the affected nodes and a short tcpdump snippet? Are these VXLAN/Geneve overlays or straight L2?

alex: tcpdump excerpt: 

    09:12:14.123456 IP 10.10.5.12.52014 > 10.10.7.33.50051: Flags [P.], seq 12345:13500, ack 54321, win 65535, length 1455
    09:12:14.123458 IP 10.10.5.12 > 10.10.7.33: Fragmented IP protocol (proto 6) 
    09:12:14.123460 IP 10.10.5.12.52014 > 10.10.7.33.50051: Flags [.], seq 12345:12400, ack 54321, win 65535, length 0 (retransmit)

    Tried `sudo iperf3` between nodes — baseline latency looks fine, but large UDP/TCP chunks get fragmented and dropped.

alex: `ip link show` on node-42: 

    3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
        link/ether 02:42:ac:11:00:02 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    4: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default

priya: ah — eth0 mtu=1450, vxlan0 mtu=1500. Encapsulation is increasing packet size past node MTU -> fragmentation. Looks like CNI bumped overlay MTU but host dev left at 1450. That'll break gRPC streaming when messages exceed path MTU.

dave: Confirmed on node-43: `ip link show` shows same mismatch. NICs are Mellanox mlx5 (SR-IOV) on these nodes. We also saw GSO/GRO enabled by default. Output: 

    $ ethtool -k eth0
    offload features for eth0:
      rx-checksumming: on
      tx-checksumming: on
      scatter-gather: on
      tcp-segmentation-offload: on
      generic-segmentation-offload: on
      generic-receive-offload: on

jen: This is a known painful combo: vxlan/geneve + NIC GSO + MTU mismatch + newer kernel can cause sticky fragments where offloads emit oversized frames that don't get re-fragmented properly. Quick mitigations: 

    - set overlay device MTU to <= host eth0 MTU (e.g., vxlan0 mtu 1400)
    - disable GSO/GRO/TCO on host netdevs as a short-term workaround:

    sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off

    - or clamp CNI to advertise smaller MTU to pods in CNI config 

alex: Tried disabling GSO on node-42 — small improvement (fewer retransmits) but large streaming gRPC calls still hang intermittently for >1200B payloads. Also saw kernel dmesg logs: `mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: firmware event: bad csum on large skb` so NIC offload/kernel boundary might be producing corrupted/fragments.

priya: Can we canary rollback the kernel on one node or force CNI MTU clamp to 1400? Rolling kernel rollback probably safer short-term since firmware/kernel mismatch looks plausible.

dave: I'll kick off a canary rollback on node-42 and node-43, replace kernel to previous build, cordon + drain, and monitor. Rolling now, tagging @jen and @priya.

infra-bot: Rolling action started: kernel-rollback job #kb-772 on nodes [node-42,node-43]. ETA ~12m. See https://ci.internal/jobs/kb-772 :gear:

jen: After rollback results, we should: 

    - add MTU sanity check to node bootstrap (fail if overlay mtu > host mtu)
    - update CNI helm values to set `mtu: 1400` for gpu-pool overlay config
    - file bug with NIC vendor about offload/firmware interaction

alex: Thanks — after rollback node-42 shows no gRPC stalls in the 20m observation window. Opening a follow-up ticket to push MTU clamp in CNI and add a preflight check.

dave: Created ticket INFRA-2238 with the tcpdump and kernel dmesg logs, assigning to `networking` and `platform` teams. I'll keep rolling rest of the canary group.

jen: Note for postmortem: include cost impact — some streaming workloads retried extensively and caused GPU job queueing spikes; estimate +12h GPU walltime wasted across jobs.

alex: closing the loop here — will follow up in INFRA-2238 with pcap + mitigation plan. :thumbsup:
